test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The cost price of a box of notebooks is ₹7,400. The shopkeeper gave 28% discount on the cost price. What will be the selling price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is taken as 100%.

Discount = 28% of CP.

Selling Price (SP) = CP − Discount% = 100% − 28% = 72%.

SP = 7,400 × 72/100 = 74 × 72 = 5,328.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,328.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Cost Price (CP) = ₹7,400 and Discount% = 28%.

Formula Used: Selling Price = Cost Price − (Discount% × Cost Price)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c1a0e9dbb9f734b871ea80f33c38073360392a5568cfc1e4434bb48582cec35.png] 

⇒ Discount Amount = 28% of 7,400

⇒ Discount Amount = (28 ÷ 100) × 7,400

⇒ Discount Amount = 28 × 74 = 2,072

⇒ Selling Price = 7,400 − 2,072

⇒ Selling Price = 5,328

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,328.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Discount Formula

Generally, discount is offered on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, effective discount = (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100.
